quest.title: Three Wishes
quest.description: Setting foot on Inazuma's main island — Narukami Island — for the first time, you carry your Invitation Letter to Komore Teahouse, not knowing what might happen next...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x650, Primogem x30, Mora x31125, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x6

chapter.title: The Immovable God and the Eternal Euthymia

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: According to the letter, this should be the place.

dialogues.speaker: Kozue
dialogues.text: Sorry, we don't serve the general public. I'm afraid you'll have to leave.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait! We're not the general public...

dialogues.speaker: Kozue
dialogues.text: Well then... you must be a couple of wandering outlanders that snuck into the nation... judging by your attire.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Are our clothes really so— oh! Uh... What Paimon means to say is—

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Here's our Invitation Letter.

dialogues.speaker: Kozue
dialogues.text: Hmm, the Yashiro Commission's seal... this must be from Mr. Thoma. It seems there's more to you than meets the eye.

dialogues.speaker: Kozue
dialogues.text: In which case, welcome to the Komore Teahouse, a safe haven for the Yashiro Commission.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, that sounds more like it.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well, now that we're here, where's Thoma?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Paimon doesn't see him anywhere, do you think he forgot his promise to meet us?
Who forgot their promise? I was beginning to think you'd forgotten about me!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—Wh—What!? Is that dog talking to us!?
Hahaha, relax, no need to look so surprised. I take it this is the first time you've seen me in this form?

choices.text: So you're a... dog?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Huh, so you didn't see anything like this when you were in Liyue Harbor?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ah, now that you mention it, this does suddenly seem less out of the ordinary...

choices.text: But it still doesn't really add up...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Hahaha. Alright, alright, I've had my fun.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! You're this close to getting an ugly nickname, mister!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Hehe, well, I've had some time to kill, given that I've been waiting here for you for so long... as was the case in Ritou...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: So I came up with this little fun greeting for when you arrived.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: But, in all seriousness, I would like to apologize about that little "test" you went through earlier. Though it was quite necessary...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: It helped us determine whether or not to bring you before Miss Kamisato, and whether you had the courage to face the lightning alongside us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmph. Don't think that Paimon's gonna forgive you just because you're getting all serious now!

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Haha... Sorry, did I overdo it? My apologies.

choices.text: So, how did we do in our "test"?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Let me just say this, you've often found yourself skirting "the rules" from the very beginning, haven't you?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Naturally, this is due to your unwavering and resolute determination.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: A long time ago, we had a friend who was much the same... but when the lightning struck...

choices.text: You mean Kazuha's friend...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Ah, so you've heard of his story, hmm...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: His light still burns all the more brightly...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So will we be allowed to meet the Shirasagi Himegimi?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Yes, of course. I will bring you to the Kamisato residence, where the Yashiro Commission is located.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: But before that, there is one other place I was hoping you both would accompany me to.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? Where?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: I would like you to come with me to the Statue of the Omnipresent God. It's still under construction now, but you can already see it from practically anywhere on Narukami Island.

choices.text: You mean he died in a duel before the throne...
"The courage to face the lightning"...?
I know a dog when I see one.
Where did the human-looking Thoma go?

talks.objective: Go to the Statue of the Omnipresent God

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This area sure feels gloomy. People probably don't come here often, do they?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh, are Paimon's eyes playing tricks, or are there things embedded in the statue...?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Visions.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Visions! You mean all the Visions that are collected from the Vision Hunt Decree are put into this statue!?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: So you've already heard of the Vision Hunt Decree.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why did the shogun issue the Vision Hunt Decree?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Before I try to explain, I should perhaps remind you first that Mondstadt is the City of Freedom, and Liyue is the City of Contracts...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: As for Inazuma... It's known as the Nation of Eternity.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: The Raiden Shogun is both the nation's most powerful ruler, and its deity.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: The "eternity" in question... is her endless and unchanging will to rule over Inazuma.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: As such, she relies on the Tri-Commission to regulate the nation's affairs, and the Sakoku Decree to limit the people's movement.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: The shogun wishes to keep Inazuma in stasis, allowing the stream of time to flow from one end to the other without disturbing it, for all time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Seems like every god has their own will...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Of course, this is my own limited understanding. As for the reason behind the recent Vision Hunt Decree...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Perhaps the shogun believes that Visions grant people the power to change, and that her eternity doesn't allow for such instability to exist.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Whatever the case, the fact is that the Raiden Shogun has dispatched the Tenryou Commission to scour the nation for Visions, embedding each one in this statue...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: ... and this Statue of the Omnipresent God can be seen as Inazuma's symbol of eternity.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But if that's the case, wouldn't you say that the Raiden Shogun is being... I don't know, selfish?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Haha, only outlanders such as yourselves would ever dare speak out so directly against the Raiden Shogun.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: And yet... I agree. The Vision Hunt Decree is something that simply should not exist, and Miss Kamisato has been committed to fighting it since the day it was announced.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Huh? {NICKNAME}, are you okay? You look like your mind is elsewhere.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Sound? What sound? I didn't hear anything... did something happen?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What was that... sound just now?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, you touched the statue, and then... and then what?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I could hear the sound of... people's aspirations.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: "Aspirations"?

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Hmm... That would seem to confirm the saying.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Have you heard it before? That when a person's ambition reaches a certain strength, the gods look upon them with favor.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: That is where Visions come from... In other words, a person's Vision represents their ambition.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: So, if what you just said is true...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: ...then the ambitions of these people are stronger than I imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So a Vision symbolizes ambition, and not power...

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Alright. Time for the next stop on our tour of Narukami Island: the Kamisato residence.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew, finally!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So this is the kind of place where the big shots of Inazuma live, huh? Paimon kinda expected it to be... snazzier.

choices.text: It's hard to top the Jade Chamber.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Welcome, at last, to the Kamisato residence, honored guests. Miss Kamisato is delighted to finally meet you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Is this the Shirasagi Himegimi you keep going on about? So, uh, where's she at?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Ahem...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... uh, behind the screen?

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Yes, haha, as the daughter of the Yashiro Commission, this is how Miss Kamisato is accustomed to receiving guests.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: Consider it a time-honored tradition within the Yashiro Commission. Forgive me if this is an unwelcome surprise.

choices.text: I think I understand.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Makes sense, she's a super-important person after all.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Please forgive my lack of courtesy for receiving you in this fashion... especially following such a long and wearisome journey over the sea.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I have awaited your arrival with great anticipation, and Thoma assures me that you do indeed possess the power to change the tide of the times.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: At present in Inazuma, in the name of the Vision Hunt Decree, the people's aspirations are being senselessly trampled underfoot.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Though the Yashiro Commission serves the shogun, it is the people with whom we share close bonds, given the contact we are required to have with them in the performance of our duties.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: A commission's power rises and falls with the trust of their people. Thus, we cannot remain indifferent to this situation without also remaining indifferent to our own fate.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Traveler, lend us your power, and we can—

choices.text: I'm just here to meet the Raiden Shogun.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Oh...

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: See, milady, it's just like I said... this will take us nowhere...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I'm going to leave now.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: No, please... wait! Please... Don't go...

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: *sigh*

response.speaker: Player
response.text: What?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: I will introduce you to the Raiden Shogun, on one condition... You must fulfill three small wishes on my behalf.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What are your wishes?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: They pertain to three whose Visions were taken from them... Perhaps once you've met them, you will understand...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: A warrior who guards a village, a former samurai who helped carry out the Vision Hunt Decree, and a swordmaster determined to become the best in the world... Does Paimon got that right?

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Correct. Please do all you can to help them. I will await your return here.

choices.text: I will do as you wish.

response.speaker: Kamisato Ayaka
response.text: Hehe... Then, you have my gratitude.

response.speaker: Thoma
response.text: I'm sure you'll do great.

choices.text: This is a tall order...
I did not come to start a rebellion.
(This is slightly anticlimactic...)
It's hard to top the Dawn Winery.

dialogues.speaker: Thoma
dialogues.text: Miss Kamisato's left, it seems. No cutting corners, now, okay?

dialogues.speaker: Kozue
dialogues.text: It's been quite some time since I've seen anyone show up with a new Invitation Letter. I wish you two luck.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's your work coming along?

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: I wrote a little when the inspiration hit, but I feel like... Um, this is rather embarrassing...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mind reading it out to me?

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Sure! As... as long as you don't laugh... heh.

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text:
"You and I
Like the stars and moon
The wind and the clouds
Like flowers and mist
Never shall we part."

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: H—How is it... Will it do?

choices.text: Seems a little plain.

response.speaker: Marvin
response.text: Is that so? Hmm, I thought so too... I've got to practice more so that I can write Marla a better poem.

response.speaker: Marvin
response.text: Thanks! I'll make some edits before handing this in. Please give me a while more, Professor Venti!

choices.text: Expressive, if a bit immature.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's your work coming along?

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean the homework that Professor Venti gave us...

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it! Even though preparing a gift for Barbara-sama is my top priority, creating a poem filled with passion is just as important!

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: Let me show you the power of a fan's heart!

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text:
"No further distance in this world below
Wider even than life and death
Than that of the Cathedral window
You within — I, outside left"

choices.text: Not bad, though it's kind of ordinary.

response.speaker: Albert
response.text: *sigh* It seems that you lack spirit — you still do not understand the regard in which we hold Barbara-sama.

response.speaker: Albert
response.text: But it's fine, you have much time ahead of you. Good luck, Traveler!

response.speaker: Albert
response.text: Let me give this a bit more thought and come up with a better version, and then I can submit it to Professor Venti.

choices.text: How about not peeping next time, eh?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How's your work coming along?

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean the love poem I'm writing for Master Jean! I—I'm still working on it!

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: Professor Venti was teaching us tricks for writing love poems, yes, but what I'd like to express is more like admiration and yearning.

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: I did write a poem, but I haven't had the time to send it to the Professor just yet... Would you like to hear it?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Lay it on me.

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: "Your earnest profile working\nLike the moon in the night sky gleaming\nIt leads me into restful dreaming"

dialogues.speaker: Ellin
dialogues.text: How is it? Will it do?

choices.text: I can feel your sincerity!

response.speaker: Ellin
response.text: Really? That's great! That's exactly what I'd like to express!

response.speaker: Ellin
response.text: Thank you! I'll make a few more improvements, and then I'll hand it in.

choices.text: Very passionate indeed...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you around!

dialogues.speaker: Plauen
dialogues.text: See you. Come back and challenge this domain again if you have the time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you know about any of the other activities?

dialogues.speaker: Plauen
dialogues.text: Hmm, for this, you can go look for Lizzie. She's always introducing fun events to people during the Windblume Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Plauen
dialogues.text: I hope that you'll enjoy yourself, too!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's in this domain?

dialogues.speaker: Plauen
dialogues.text: This is a special domain that was discovered by the Adventurers' Guild some time ago. It seems to only turn up at specific times.

dialogues.speaker: Plauen
dialogues.text: There are quite a few interesting things going on inside. We've opened it to the public after some modification work.

dialogues.speaker: Plauen
dialogues.text: If you're interested, please feel free to attempt this challenge. Do it alone, or call your friends, either is fine!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It's not dangerous in there, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Plauen
dialogues.text: Don't worry, we'll have seasoned adventurers accompanying you all the way if you bring people without any experience.

dialogues.speaker: Plauen
dialogues.text: But I think that a veteran such as you will be fine.

dialogues.speaker: Plauen
dialogues.text: Give it a go! This is the special festive event that the Adventurers' Guild has prepared for everyone.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Lizzie
dialogues.text: See you. Happy Windblume Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you do here?

dialogues.speaker: Lizzie
dialogues.text: I'm in charge of welcoming guests, and of organizing all sorts of fun activities for everyone during the Windblume Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Lizzie
dialogues.text: A lot of the events are being held outdoors due to the large area needed, so without a guide to tell them where things are happening, lots of people are going to miss out!

dialogues.speaker: Lizzie
dialogues.text: And I, Lizzie, am glad to step up to that plate!

choices.text: So what's going on, then?

response.speaker: Lizzie
response.text: There are three events taking place during the festival: "Bullseye Balloons," "Floral Freefall," and "Ballads of Breeze".

response.speaker: Lizzie
response.text: As for the details... As opposed to having me explain, I think it might be easier if you try them out yourself.

response.speaker: Lizzie
response.text: As long as the preparations for the activity have already been made, I can tell you where they're being held.

response.speaker: Lizzie
response.text: May you have a happy Windblume Festival!

choices.text: Are there any other interesting things to do?

response.speaker: Lizzie
response.text: I've heard that the Adventurers' Guild has something special up their sleeve for the Windblume Festival.

response.speaker: Lizzie
response.text: If you're interested, I'd advise you to look for an adventurer named Plauen. He'll tell you all about it!

dialogues.speaker: Lizzie
dialogues.text: Hey there! Having fun this Windblume Festival?

dialogues.speaker: Godwin
dialogues.text: *sigh* I wonder how Glory is doing...

dialogues.speaker: Godwin
dialogues.text: I wish I could return to Mondstadt to see her... But I can't. How can I let her know that her lover is a coward and a deserter?

dialogues.speaker: Godwin
dialogues.text: The best I can do now is clear out monsters and do my part to protect Mondstadt... and her.

dialogues.speaker: Godwin
dialogues.text: Laugh if you want. I'm... I'm a useless man.

dialogues.speaker: Doolan
dialogues.text: This is the time of the Windblume Festival, the season when dandelions float about in the wind.

dialogues.speaker: Doolan
dialogues.text: I've always been looking forward to a time when I might express my love for my destined one amid a sea of billowing dandelions...

dialogues.speaker: Doolan
dialogues.text: But I never expected Miss Patchi to be too absorbed in her research to understand a thing I was saying...

dialogues.speaker: Doolan
dialogues.text: Nothing could be more boring than spending such a romantic festival buried knee-deep in books ruins.

dialogues.speaker: Doolan
dialogues.text: Who knows how long it'll take for her to understand these deep yet nebulous feelings of mine...

dialogues.speaker: Patchi the Curious
dialogues.text: What sort of flower is a "Windblume"? The one who solves this particular enigma will certainly leave their mark on the academic world.

dialogues.speaker: Patchi the Curious
dialogues.text: And that's why some researchers have teamed up with adventurers to search for clues as to the "Windblume"'s identity.

dialogues.speaker: Patchi the Curious
dialogues.text: Unfortunately, they haven't made much headway.

dialogues.speaker: Patchi the Curious
dialogues.text: But we won't give up! We will find that true "Windblume." That is our solemn duty as researchers!

dialogues.speaker: Patchi the Curious
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, Mr. Doolan often tells me that we should go to Cape Oath to have a look. What a curious idea. It's not as if there are ruins there or anything...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: Indeed. No matter which camp you belong in, remember to enjoy this hard-earned freedom that we possess.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What camp do you belong to?

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: Me? I don't put much importance on what sort of flower the "Windblume" actually is.

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: I'm a researcher and writer who studies history and culture. I must maintain a neutral stance...

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: ...Opinion is the great enemy of scholarship.

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: But if you find any documents or material of historical value, you're welcome to discuss them with me.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Asterists?

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: Yes. They are also known as the "Windblume Traditionalists."

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: As opposed to a celebration of romance, they believe that the Windblume Festival is more about commemorating the liberation of Old Mondstadt from tyranny.

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: As far as I'm aware, "Windblume" was possibly once a code word for people who wished to stay in contact and plot resistance in secret...

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: But most people have forgotten this layer of meaning, and so those who feel that this festival should stand for the liberation of Mondstadt have become the minority.

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: Windwheel Asters bear the title of "the visible winds," and so the traditionalists have chosen it to represent them.

dialogues.speaker: Dr. Edith
dialogues.text: Hmm, you're not celebrating the festival in the city. Are you, by any chance... an Asterist?

dialogues.speaker: Myweiss
dialogues.text: The Windblume Festival... Hmph, it's that time of the year again, is it?

dialogues.speaker: Myweiss
dialogues.text: I had an epiphany when I got divorced, and it was like waking from a long dream: the Windblume Festival should never have been associated with love at all!

dialogues.speaker: Myweiss
dialogues.text: Hah, it must have been the scheme of some scheming city merchants. Wouldn't they love to package every festival as something for lovers?

dialogues.speaker: Myweiss
dialogues.text: ...People in love have no rational thought to speak of. A little flattery here and there and their wallets open wide.

dialogues.speaker: Myweiss
dialogues.text: Whatever the case, I've come to my senses now. These festivals are absolutely meaningless.

dialogues.speaker: Myweiss
dialogues.text: ...And if not for the Windblume Festival, would I even have met that man? Hmph...

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: It's Windblume Festival again... I suppose the Windblumes must be dandelions, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: No matter how strong the wind, it can only blow dandelions away, but it will never cause them to perish.

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: But this is just my opinion. But it may be for this reason that dandelions became the symbols of love.

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: I hope... I hope that our love will be just as resilient.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: Indeed, see you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the foxes...

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: Oh! As Springvale hunters, this is one of our customs.

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: Every Windblume Festival, young hunters like me go to Wolvendom to catch foxes.

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: When we catch one, we place a wreath of flowers on its head and release it. It's a prayer for finding love in the year ahead...

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: Of course, only eligible young hunters like myself participate. Hunters that have already tied the knot, like Draff for example, they're not allowed to take part.

choices.text: Did you catch a fox?

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: *sigh* Not even close. Foxes are so hard to catch.

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: I didn't catch one last Windblume Festival either. In fact, I nearly injured myself. I remember swearing that this time would be different...

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: ...and yet, low and behold, I've been outfoxed again. All I caught were a couple of squirrels.

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: That said... I wonder if Miss Sucrose could use her bio-alchemy to change squirrels into foxes?

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: I bet she could, haha...

choices.text: So everyone that catches a fox will find love?

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: Uh... if you always participate, your chances will increase exponentially...

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: ...in that sense, you're bound to bump into the right person eventually...

response.speaker: Allan
response.text: ...ahem. Anyway, that's what Draff's always telling us.

dialogues.speaker: Allan
dialogues.text: Foxes really are too difficult to catch. Just how exactly did the elders manage it...

dialogues.speaker: Six-Fingered José
dialogues.text: #Hey there, {M#amigo}{F#amiga}! Are you here to listen to Six-Fingered José's latest composition?

dialogues.speaker: Six-Fingered José
dialogues.text: Hehe, fear not. My creations do not disappoint.

dialogues.speaker: Six-Fingered José
dialogues.text: When it comes to the Windblume Festival, other bards think love songs. Madre mía, no sense of invention...

dialogues.speaker: Six-Fingered José
dialogues.text: I, Six-Fingered José, on the other hand, am not constrained by convention. I wish to eulogize the heroic epics of ages past! The people must remember that this is a day for commemorating heroes and resisting tyrants!

dialogues.speaker: Six-Fingered José
dialogues.text: Even if, ahem... I haven't quite finished the last part yet. But once it's complete, it will bring my audience running back!

dialogues.speaker: Glory
dialogues.text: Huh? I recognize that voice... Traveler?

dialogues.speaker: Glory
dialogues.text: The Windblume festivities are in full swing! If you get time, do make sure to roam around. You'll find a very different Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Glory
dialogues.text: Even better, if there's someone important to you, you should spend the festival with them. That's where the Windblume feeling truly resides...

dialogues.speaker: Glory
dialogues.text: I always used to spend the Windblume Festival with my family and my darling Godwin. How I cherish those sweet times...

dialogues.speaker: Glory
dialogues.text: I still don't know how he's getting on... May the winds protect him.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm afraid I don't know either...

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: Hmm... I wonder how Barbara-sama will react when she sees our gift...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: A letter?

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: Not a bad choice, but if it's just an ordinary letter then it'll be forgotten in no time...

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: Hmm, the content has to be different from a normal letter, we need something unforgettable...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Flowers?

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: Flowers... a—as a matter of fact... we at the Barbara Fan Club already have a similar idea.

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: Sending flowers the old-fashioned way would be too boring, better to come up with something a little more... unique...

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: I hope Barbara-sama will like what we've prepared...

dialogues.speaker: Albert
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* Traveler, what kind of gift do you think moves people the most?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Thanks, no need...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Aww, don't be shy.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Windblume Festival...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: The Windblume Festival had a very solemn meaning once...

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: But nowadays, many people believe that it's just a time when they send flowers to others and get their feelings across.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Oh? Have someone you'd like to send flowers to, do you? Let me guess... is it me, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: ...Haha, don't be so nervous. I was just joking.

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: Since it's the Windblume Festival, would you like to come to The Cat's Tail and have a few drinks?

dialogues.speaker: Margaret
dialogues.text: I might even give you some flowers... Hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Marla, the Windblume Festival is here, and yet, it holds no meaning for me...

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: Oh, Marvin, say not that!

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: We do not have your father's approval, but this time for lovers is ours also...

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: No, what I mean is that as long as I am with you, every day may as well be the Windblume Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: You're right, Marvin. Our love is like the dandelions that bloom on Cape Oath...

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Marla, no... Our love should not be a thing so fragile...

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: No, I mean to say that though the dandelions are scattered by the wild winds, their lives will not thusly end.

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: Dandelion Seeds will fly to distant places, take root, and sprout there... One day, they will cover the length and breadth of Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Oh, my darling Marla...

dialogues.speaker: Marla
dialogues.text: Oh, Marvin! My love...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll leave you to it, then.

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Yes, alright. Please don't disturb me any further...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Something on your mind?

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: I... I have a friend. Yes, a friend...

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: He's very taken with a certain girl, but unfortunately, she doesn't come from a particularly wealthy family, so my friend's rather worried that his father will oppose their marriage.

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Thing is, he truly loves that girl and wants her to be his wife.

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: So I... well, he, is wondering if he should simply come clean with his father...

choices.text: You sure you're talking about a friend?

response.speaker: Marvin
response.text: Ahem! *cough* D—Don't you say such scurrilous things...

response.speaker: Marvin
response.text: Wait a moment, you haven't been sent by the old man to test me, have you?

response.speaker: Marvin
response.text: Hmph, whatever. I said nothing. Just go.

choices.text: I don't think you should...

response.speaker: Marvin
response.text: Hmm, is that so...

response.speaker: Marvin
response.text: *cough* Ah, uh. I said nothing. You didn't hear anything from me!

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: Ugh, should I tell my father or not?

dialogues.speaker: Marvin
dialogues.text: No, I suppose it would be best if I didn't. But if I don't tell him, I...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Luke
dialogues.text: *cough* Just go...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Not going to see the sights?

dialogues.speaker: Luke
dialogues.text: Wh—What? I couldn't possibly do that. I've been tasked by a diplomat to guard the embassy. How could I just desert my post?

dialogues.speaker: Luke
dialogues.text: *cough* And even if I did want to go for a stroll, I'd have to wait for there to be no one about...

dialogues.speaker: Luke
dialogues.text: ...Hey. Don't you even think of getting me to talk. I won't shirk my duties!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Windblume Festival...

dialogues.speaker: Luke
dialogues.text: That Viktor keeps saying that this place is as boring as ever, but I can certainly feel the festive atmosphere.

dialogues.speaker: Luke
dialogues.text: I'll have you know that I take the greatest pleasure from watching the dejection of those imbeciles who confess their feelings come the festival, only to be rejected. Hah...

dialogues.speaker: Luke
dialogues.text: *cough* But back on topic, there's one thing that I don't get...

dialogues.speaker: Luke
dialogues.text: ...How did this commemorative festival become a day for lovers, anyway?

dialogues.speaker: Luke
dialogues.text: Is this what the people of Mondstadt call "freedom"?

dialogues.speaker: Luke
dialogues.text: Mondstadt only really gets interesting during festivals, anyway...

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: Nowadays, no one truly knows what the Windblume is.

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: There are some who have judged that the flower simply does not exist, save in legend and song only.

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: The way I see it, Windblumes are real so long as there are those who believe in it.

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: As to which flower it might be, I think that everyone is free to decide that for themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: I believe that this "freedom to choose" is what Lord Barbatos would have wished for us to have...

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: Nowadays, no one truly knows what the Windblume is.

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: There are some who have judged that the flower simply does not exist, save in legend and song only.

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: The way I see it, Windblumes are real so long as there are those who believe in it.

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: As to which flower it might be, I think that everyone is free to decide that for themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Grace
dialogues.text: I believe that this "freedom to choose" is what Lord Barbatos would have wished for us to have...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: A youngster like you should be more energetic. Don't be cold!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, about Stormterror's Lair...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Ah, the Windblume Festival has its origins in Old Mondstadt and the days of the Lord of the Tower. Nowadays, no one knows what the Windblume truly is.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: And that is why we explore ancient ruins to uncover the history of resistance in those days. We wish to uncover the truth behind the Windblume.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: It is a shame that few young people agree with our views...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: If you ask me, the Windblume Festival should be about recounting the era of the Tower of Storms, and the legend of that heroic rebellion, haha!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Windblume Festival...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: This is a day to remember those heroes who fought for their freedom. It is said that they once used Windblume as their code word...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: As to which flower the Windblume really is? Ah, there are as many views as there are people.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: To commemorate the courage and sacrifice of those heroes, we go out to search for clues regarding the Windblume each time the festival rolls back around.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Over many years of searching, I have come to believe more and more that the Windblume is the Windwheel Aster!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: The Windwheel Aster?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Yes! Don't you think so, too?

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Compared to the dandelion, the Windwheel Asters that turn with the wind are the true symbol of Mondstadt's freedom and the soul of the Windblume Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: It's just that we lack concrete evidence with which to convince other people...

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: Well then! It's the Windblume Festival. What do you say to going to Stormterror's Lair to search for clues regarding the Windblume?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you around.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: Happy Windblume Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Windblume Festival...

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: When we speak of the Windblume Festival, the topic of the Windblume's legend is an inevitable one.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: The Windblume Festival has its origins in Old Mondstadt, and people all have their own opinions concerning the true identity of the Windblume.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: At the moment, the two most popular must be the "Dandelionite" and "Asterist" schools of thought.

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: Of course, there are those who believe that neither of these is the true Windblume...

choices.text: About the Dandelionites...

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: Oh, they believe that the Dandelion is the Windblume. I believe that this is the most mainstream line of thinking.

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: The Dandelionites believe that the Windblume Festival is a festival for lovers and that they should express their love with the most extravagant sincerity during this time.

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: Passionate people in love will often travel to Cape Oath and express their feelings for one another amid the billowing Dandelions and profuse Cecilias...

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: It's all rather romantic, wouldn't you say?

choices.text: Then, about the Asterists...

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: Those who believe that the Windwheel Aster is the Windblume are certainly not few, but they are not as numerous as those who believe it is the Dandelion.

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: They believe that the liberation of Old Mondstadt from tyranny should be at the heart of the festival...

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: ...And that instead of celebrating love, this festival is more suited to remembrance.

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: If you think about it, this view does have its merits as well...

response.speaker: Lawrence
response.text: But it isn't the majority. I guess people just want to have a relaxing, good time during the festive season...

dialogues.speaker: Lawrence
dialogues.text: Welcome to Mondstadt — make sure you don't miss out on the Windblume Festival.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've got other things to attend to.

dialogues.speaker: Goth
dialogues.text: I see. Be careful out there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Windblume Festival...

dialogues.speaker: Goth
dialogues.text: Oh, my, if it isn't the Windblume Festival again. The youth of the city have come out to play.

dialogues.speaker: Goth
dialogues.text: Haha. I wonder what flower shall be offered up to the Anemo Archon this year? Will it still be a Dandelion?

dialogues.speaker: Goth
dialogues.text: When I was a young man, I used to enjoy debating the identity of the Windblume as well. I was quite the dyed-in-the-wool Dandelionite.

dialogues.speaker: Goth
dialogues.text: Come to think of it, my wife and I met during the Windblume Festival. It was truly love at first sight...

dialogues.speaker: Goth
dialogues.text: *sigh* How the years have gone by since then...

dialogues.speaker: Goth
dialogues.text: #Excuse me, {M#sir}{F#ma'am}? ...Oh, er, I mean hey there, friend! Why, this work mode of mine... So, care for a chat?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Bruce
dialogues.text: Okay, goodbye!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's with the long face?

dialogues.speaker: Bruce
dialogues.text: Ah, it's just a shame. Mondstadt is so... well, it's peaceful, but maybe it's too much so.

dialogues.speaker: Bruce
dialogues.text: *sigh* If only I'd been born in the days of Old Mondstadt *hic* ...just maybe...

dialogues.speaker: Bruce
dialogues.text: How is one to become a hero in such days of peace?

choices.text: By fending Stormterror off, perchance?

response.speaker: Bruce
response.text: Well, that certainly was an opportunity, but...

response.speaker: Bruce
response.text: Wait. Are you trying to ask me what I was doing during the Stormterror Crisis?

response.speaker: Bruce
response.text: I... I'll have you know that I was doing a sweeping survey of all of Mondstadt's safety blind spots!

response.speaker: Bruce
response.text: *cough* I mean, it's all water under the bridge now, isn't it? Let's not dredge it up anymore, hahaha...

choices.text: Perhaps dueling a Fatui Harbinger might do the trick?

response.speaker: Bruce
response.text: I... well... I mean, Snezhnaya is, after all, an ally of Mondstadt's...

response.speaker: Bruce
response.text: I couldn't possibly cause a diplomatic incident just like that, could I?

response.speaker: Bruce
response.text: *cough* I guess I should just find some other way to do this...

dialogues.speaker: Bruce
dialogues.text: Ah, the Windblume Festival... How I envy those heroes who left their mark on history...

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: I wonder who will have the honor of offering the Windblume to Lord Barbatos this year?

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: Ah, I'm so envious. If only I could be the one. Everyone's eyes would be on me...

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: (And who knows? Maybe Diluc might notice me if I'm the one offering flowers...)

dialogues.speaker: Donna
dialogues.text: (That would be so wonderful... Oh gosh, he's all I can think about, isn't he...)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I've got to go.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: I hope you'll enjoy yourself during the Windblume festivities.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Windblume Festival...

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: The Windblume Festival is an ancient tradition of Mondstadt's. A day for freedom and romance.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: When we speak of Windblume Festival tradition, I suppose it's about giving the "Windblume" in your heart to the person who's the most important to you, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: As to what flower the Windblume actually is, everyone's got their own opinions.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Well, that's freedom for you, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'd like to buy some flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Certainly. We have a fine selection, whether you're looking to give a bouquet to someone or even do some gardening yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Flora
dialogues.text: Welcome to Floral Whisper. Are you looking to get someone a bouquet? It's the Windblume Festival, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Goodbye.

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: Take care, and make sure to enjoy the Windblume Festival!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: About the Windblume Festival and adventurers...

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: A lot of couples will choose to have dates at Cape Oath, but there are some brave adventurer couples who will venture near Stormterror's Lair.

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: That area is simply crawling with monsters, so many adventurers will come here to purchase new equipment...

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: ...After all, if you were to be beaten by monsters in that place, you wouldn't just lose face — you'd be putting your companion in danger, too...

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: So each time the Windblume Festival rolls around, we smiths run brisker business than usual, so I suppose we can be thankful for that.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What do you have to sell?

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: Take your pick from this selection. All Master's own handiwork, so you won't find any second-rate items here.

dialogues.speaker: Schulz
dialogues.text: Well, by the looks of you, I'd say you're an adventurer! Not going to stock up on some new equipment?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: *hic* A... Another!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who's she?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Oh, you mean Bea?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Dunno what she's thinking.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Ever since the Windblume Festival began, she's been bugging me about Cape Oath and heart-shaped Sunsettias...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Sunsettias of that kind just don't exist...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: You'd agree, right? *hic*

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Who are you?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: *hic* Oh, it's you...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: That's right. I'm Quinn of Quinn's Fruit. My booth is at...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Fresh fruits only at... Quinn's Fruit...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Wait... Have we met before?

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: (I'm feeling light-headed...)

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Even if she's a close friend, my resolve won't be shaken... *hic*

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: I'm being serious, there really are heart-shaped Sunsettias around Cape Oath...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Bea, your eyes must have been playing tricks on you. Sunsettias just don't grow into that shape. It's against the laws of nature.

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: And even if they did exist, there's no way that they could be sweeter than the ones I'm already selling.

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: Well, why don't we just go over to Cape Oath to have a look? It won't take long...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: No. This has to do with my convictions! Using visual attraction to sell fruit is just a cheap trick. I would never do that.

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: ...Oh come on, why won't you just get it already...

dialogues.speaker: Quinn
dialogues.text: Hmm? Come again?

dialogues.speaker: Beatrice
dialogues.text: *cough* Uh, nothing... Come on, just consider it for a second!
